law: The evidence pack a NEW_SUPERTABLE_COLUMN_CANDIDATE must carry before it may be proposed as a supertable column. Adding a column is promote-class, so the bar is evidence a reviewer can CHECK without re-deriving it: two independent publishers, their measured pairwise agreement, a crossed control ruling out the obvious alternative reading, a bound or identity the values satisfy on each publisher independently, and who would supply it over how many rows.
why_this_file_exists: The disposition's reason text has always said candidates route 'through the census + demand join (24.4), never ad-hoc'. Until 2026-07-31 that phrase appeared ONLY in the two strings asserting it -- no module, no ledger, no counter -- so ~414 candidates across the programme had no queue and could not be burned down, and def_interception_long reached full evidence with nowhere to file it.
status_is_derived: column_demand.evaluate() is the ONLY thing that sets EVIDENCED. A hand-typed status is forbidden: six nflcom families sat PENDING_CROSSWALK for days after their receipt PASSED because a generator short-circuited on a typed string before the receipt gate ran.

bar.independence: publishers must span >= 2 lineage roots per lineage_roots.v1.json; note the DECLARED_UNRECEIPTED elias_gsis_gamebook ancestor means pfr/nflcom/nflverse independence is itself unreceipted (OQ-LR-1), so an EVIDENCED status here is a DEFINITION claim -- two sources report the same number -- not a claim of independent corroboration

demands.rationale: v26 carries SEVEN *_long columns (fg, kickoff_return, passing, punt, punt_return, receiving, rushing) and no defensive one, while holding def_interception_yards and def_int_ret_td.
demands.crossed_control: Against nflcom `lng` the PFR SEASON yardage total reads 52.77% where PFR's own long reads 99.23% -- a 46-point margin. The 52.77% is itself explained: on a one-interception season the long IS the total.
demands.constraint: BOUND lng <= season interception-return yards holds independently on both publishers: 99.13% (nflcom) and 98.97% (PFR) of 15,468. SELF-CHECK: on seasons with exactly one interception, lng == yds on 98.82% of 4,985.

lower_layer_denominator.reason: PFR's lower-layer def_int has one 2025 mismatch (1532/1533); the long counter cannot clear until the denominator is reconciled.

demands.rationale: punt-coverage family; v26 carries no coverage-side punting columns at all.
demands.crossed_control: The same join and the same 1,940 rows match `rety` to a DIFFERENT PFR column (punt_ret_yds_opp, 96.19%), so the join is not agreeing with everything indiscriminately.
demands.constraint: BOUND tb <= punts on the nflcom side; punts itself is a licensed mapping at 0.9966.

demands.rationale: the standard punt-placement statistic; v26 has no coverage-side punting.

demands.rationale: net punting is the coverage-adjusted total; v26 carries gross punt_yards only.
demands.constraint: BOUND net_yds <= punt_yards (gross); punt_yards is a licensed mapping at 0.9797.

lower_layer_denominator.reason: gross punt_yards is below the 0.995 quality bar; net yards cannot clear against an unstable lower layer.

demands.rationale: v26 carries the kickoff RETURN side and nothing for the kicking side. A touchback is the modern kickoff's most common outcome, so its absence makes kickoff volume uninterpretable.
demands.crossed_control: fgm -> fgm on the SAME join agrees 100.00% (n=2,596), so the crosswalk and the per-team dedupe are not the source of any disagreement here.

lower_layer_denominator.reason: no receipted lower-layer kickoffs counter is currently registered; the bound is only prose until that counter is measured.

demands.rationale: The PUNTING team's coverage result. v26 carries punt_return_yards (the returner's stat) and nothing for yards allowed, which is what evaluates a punter's coverage unit and is the operand net punting is built from.
demands.crossed_control: punts -> punt on the SAME join agrees 99.56% (n=2,712). And rety is POSITIVELY IDENTIFIED as the allowed side rather than assumed: its block-mates `ret` and `td` were withdrawn from the returner-side canonicals at 0.00% and 67.34%, so the block is the coverage block.
demands.constraint: punt_return_yards_allowed >= 0; may be negative in the source on a single season (eg -7) where returns lost yardage

lower_layer_denominator.reason: the candidate is a coverage-side yard counter, but no lower-layer coverage-volume receipt proves its denominator/constraint yet.

demands.rationale: Average kickoff distance. IDENTITY IS CONFIRMED, the agreement is not: median difference against PFR kickoff_yds_avg is 0.0 and 84.15% land within 1.0 yard, but only 22.96% within 0.05. Both publish one decimal over slightly different kickoff sets, and PFR's own published avg does not equal its own yds/ko either (57.03%). This is a rate-tolerance question, not a mapping question.

agreement.note: within 1.0 yard: 0.8415; median diff 0.0; two-sided (nflcom higher 886, PFR higher 631)

demands.crossed_control: Restricting to SINGLE-TEAM seasons moved it 0.2448 -> 0.2513, which refutes per-team rate summing as the cause. Medians 61.4 (nflcom) vs 62.0 (PFR) confirm the column is kickoff distance, not return average (avg_2 medians 21.4).
demands.constraint: a kickoff averages ~55-70 yards; nflcom max 247.9 exceeds any possible single-kick distance and is itself a defect to explain
demands.supply: pfr_player_kicking.kickoff_yds + .kickoff give the operands nflcom lacks

demands.rationale: Net punting average. Joe: one of three published rates carrying NO equation floor. Measured against PFR punt_net_yds_per_punt at 65.37% on single-team seasons -- too low to promote and too high to dismiss; the two publishers likely differ on the touchback penalty in the numerator.
demands.crossed_control: its OPERAND net_yds -> punt_net_yds agrees 95.62% on the same join, so the numerator is sound and the disagreement is in the rate definition
demands.supply: derive from punt_net_yards / punts once net_yards is promoted
